Senses.Explanation: To put understanding to immediate use in one's course of ongoing course, commonly opposed to letting it circulate at the level of conventional discourse. Guizong Zhichang explicitly contrasts understanding, which permits use on the way, with failure to understand, which leaves conventional circulation. Yuanwu Keqin compares such use to a dragon gaining water and a tiger leaning on a mountain. Zhenjing Kewen says that understanding yields use on the way and then asks what transmission would be if it were not such use. Jingzhao warns beginners to return to the source and not seek use on the way, showing the phrase can name a tempting pragmatic appropriation rather than an unconditional good.
